Example 2.5.2.1: cell means as estimable functions

Source: R/examples.R
Examp2.5.2.1.Rd

The four drug-by-dose means of ex125 (25.45, 24.28, 21.48 and 17.13) and their variance 1.27, as least-squares means.

References

Duchateau, L., Janssen, P. and Rowlands, G. J. (1998). Linear Mixed Models. An Introduction with Applications in Veterinary Research. International Livestock Research Institute, Nairobi.

See also

vlm_lsmeans, ex125

Other VetResearchLMM examples: Examp1.3.2, Examp2.2.1.7, Examp2.3.2, Examp2.4.2.2, Examp2.4.3.1, Examp2.5.1.1, Examp2.5.3.1, Examp2.5.4.1, Examp2.6.1, Examp3.1, Examp3.2, Examp3.3

Author

Muhammad Yaseen (myaseen208@gmail.com)

Examples

# SAS program of the book (Appendix B):
#   proc mixed data=ex125;
#     class drug dose region;
#     model pcv = drug dose drug*dose;
#     random region drug*region;
#     lsmeans drug*dose;
#   run;

fm <-
  vlm_fit(
      fixed    = Pcv ~ Drug + dose + Drug:dose
    , data     = ex125
    , random   = ~ Region + Region:Drug
    , repeated = NULL
    , method   = "REML"
    , ddfm     = "default"
    , type     = 3
    , class    = NULL
    , bound    = TRUE
    , control  = list()
    )
vlm_lsmeans(
    fit    = fm
  , specs  = ~ Drug:dose
  , at     = NULL
  , diff   = FALSE
  , adjust = "none"
  , level  = 0.95
  )
#> Least-squares means (denominator df: contain; 95% limits)
#> 
#> Least squares means
#>     Drug dose estimate    se df     t      p lower upper
#>  BERENIL    h    25.45 1.128 10 22.56 <1e-04 22.94 27.96
#>  BERENIL    l    24.28 1.128 10 21.53 <1e-04 21.77 26.80
#>  samorin    h    21.48 1.128 10 19.05 <1e-04 18.97 24.00
#>  samorin    l    17.13 1.128 10 15.19 <1e-04 14.62 19.65
#> 
#> Sources: Duchateau, Janssen and Rowlands (1998); Searle, Speed and Milliken
#> (1980). Full references: vlm_cite(x).
